optional.--save: GIL input, paired with --terrain-id; exclusive with --run
optional.--terrain-id: integer terrain ID; required for --save, optional check for --run
optional.--run: successful original terrain receipt; independently decoded full after, not an unchecked sidecar

required.--output: new .runtime JSON path containing the generated edits array

newOptional.--shapes-guard: boolean; expired write fixture containing all three slope types plus path; excludes inspect/runtime/catalog-probe/refresh

plan.compatible: --edits may contain op=surface; outputs native-terrain-plan-v3 when present; --catalog-run remains available

batch-create.compatible: --edits may contain op=surface; each card carries shapeSemantics and uses original accepted after as next before

cellSchema.slope: null removes slope; object {type:1|2|3,direction:'z+'|'x+'|'z-'|'x-'} sets native shape
cellSchema.path: boolean creates/removes native path; no arbitrary integer accepted
cellSchema.height: optional native integer code; omitted preserves existing height
cellSchema.material: optional observed/catalogued material ID; slope shares base material

workflow: surface-edits emits op=surface; it neither edits a GIL nor accesses the game.
Use plan --save FORMAL --terrain-id ID --edits FILE --output PLAN; use batch-create for many cards. New cells require height and material; existing unspecified fields are retained.

Single plan: fresh scene inspect -> prepare --baseline FRESH --plan PLAN -> execute. Multi-card: fresh scene baseline A -> prepare --baseline A --inspect-only --terrain-id ID -> execute inspect -> later fresh scene baseline B -> batch-prepare --baseline B --inspection INSPECT_RUN -> execute -> batch-accept. Repeat with fresh cards; accepted original full after supplies next before.

Before any transaction, the native card verifies complete cells, exact shape code/guards and actual material style/prefab resources. The normal snapshot/SetCell/notify/close/owner-rebuild chain runs, then resources and full after are checked again.

Explicit native save and verify-save --save-run (or batch-verify-save) prove persistence. --after remains content-only. Runtime Renderer/ray queries and player traversal are separate acceptance layers.
boundaries: Native types1/2/3 and their preview codes are verified; front/left/right label-to-ID correspondence remains unverified, and no label alias is guessed.
Directions use local terrain axes, not assumed world axes; use the existing catalog/calibration matrix for world conversion.
Shape brushes retain height. Prefabs provide slopes, not arbitrary continuous heights or custom vertices.
Water is never silently cleared: slope operations and path creation reject water. Path removal preserves it.
Changing/removing a slope on a path requires explicit path:false. Creating a path over an existing slope is a separate accepted card, matching native path preservation.
Loaded path resource directories are checked; this alone does not prove every rendered mask, pixels, player traversal or reopen.
